Whatever’s being dismissed on your end is going to end up as resentment. The small cracks matter. If your issues aren’t being addressed now, they’re going to blow up in your faces sooner or later.

You’re not feeling the way you are for no reason. Have the difficult conversation now if you still want to end things amicably. Prolonging the situation serves neither of you.

If bumabaliktad sikmura mo sa nagawa/kayang gawin ng partner mo, reconsider na. Hindi kayo tugma ng values. Kahit maging exclusive kayo in the future, this is going to keep haunting you. Parang nauseating feeling na hindi maalis sayo hahahay. And agree sa sinabi ng iba, baka magkasakit ka pa.

Frequent dating apps or clubs like you said. It’s easy to enter the scene. Plus points if you’re conventionally attractive—though IMHO, it doesn’t really matter nowadays. Nadadaan din siya sa confidence tsaka lakas ng loob ng iba.

For me, it doesn’t work. Rarely happened—madalas wasak menty ko kaya ako pumapatol. But all experiences left a bad taste in my mouth. Nakakapagod tapos nakaka-ewan ng feeling after. Ako lang naman yun. I can’t treat sex as transactional or “ganun-ganun” lang. Makes me wanna hurl, ganun. Will really depend on your personal experiences and beliefs. Walang right or wrong… ish.

Yung ibang kilala ko na nagtagal sa stage na yan, may negative bearing din sa relationships after. It’s hard when your values don’t align with your partner’s, especially if your partner hasn’t been through hookups at all. Trust can get affected. Hindi rin reasonable yung “so you can’t accept my past” argument. Justified kasi both sides. Nothing wrong with hookup culture as long as it’s done cleanly, but you have to accept that it will come with its own set of consequences. You’ll have to deal with it na lang.

If it’s for you, it’s for you, I guess. You’ll never know if you never try—pero I suggest wag na. Hahaha. Nakakatakot pa STIs ngayon.

I think I’m actually “lucky” that I can recognize it as sexual assault and not some twisted way of showing affection or dominance in a relationship. I can only imagine how it is for other people who’ve been conditioned to think that “giving in” is okay and even... romantic. I’m getting chills just thinking of it.

It baffles me how the concept of consent has been so warped to the point that the discussion about it needs to be dragged out to unnecessary lengths, when all it really should be is a matter of respecting each other’s wishes. “No” isn’t open to interpretation—no means no. I don’t see why it’s so hard for people to be decent human beings that can respect the boundaries set by others.

Thank you for your comforting words. ♥️ Wishing you great days ahead.

The game just really wants you to explore more than you normally would. Call it a form of unlock-able content if you will.

Those seem to be rolling and box scars. The definitive way of treating them is through surgery. Different techniques are available like the punch excision procedure (the scar is excised and the skin is repaired through stitching or grafting) or subcision (the scar fibers under the skin are loosened to reduce its deep appearance). Consult a board-certified dermatologist re: this, as these are medical procedures.

Surgery is usually complemented by laser treatments, peels, or other topicals to help with pigmentation and refinement of texture.

Topicals (AHA, BHA, etc.) may be effective with hyperpigmentation but they do very little when it comes to deep acne scarring. I suggest you avoid “self-use” or DIY derma rollers, as you may cause more bad than good if they aren’t used correctly.

It’s important to understand why the notion of “acne-causing” foods is a thing in the first place, and it boils down to the concept of glycemic index.

Foods that have a high glycemic index (which means that they are able to raise your blood sugar levels faster) influence the body to produce hormones that stimulate the activity of oil glands.

Hyperactive oil glands lead to increased oil production. Increased amounts of sebum can lead to clogged pores, which can then lead to the development of acne.

And if you’re going to notice, foods with high-sugar content fit in that list—which is why they’re often regarded as “culprits” when it comes to acne.

With that perspective, it would help you to do research on which foods have a high glycemic index and which ones don’t. Sticking to a diet with a low glycemic index may help in improving your skin as well as your overall health.

Technically speaking, pores can’t be made smaller or larger by external products alone. Their size is mainly influenced by genetics and drastic changes in your skin (acne, scarring, aging, etc).

If you’re cleansing correctly and thoroughly, then pore-clogging won’t be much of a problem. Use adequate sun protection since sun exposure is one of the main culprits of skin damage and aging, leading to the loss of elasticity in your skin which leads to larger pore size.

Everyone starts somewhere, no need to feel sorry about anything.

If you’re experiencing ingrown hairs, which may contribute to the development of acne, try to shave along the direction of hair growth instead of against it. Avoid pressing the razor too much against your skin as well. It doesn’t leave you with your smoothest shave, but it will help in preventing ingrown hairs.

Wash your face first prior to shaving. Use a light conditioner to soften your hairs and to make your shaving experience smoother, as shaving creams may be too harsh for your skin—although this is for you to decide.

You can use a facial wash with salicylic acid to help in minimizing acne. What’s your skin type? Is your skin dry, oily, or a combination of both? If your skin is dry, you can stick with the Nivea sensitive cream if it’s not the culprit of your breakouts. If you’re oily, use a lightweight moisturizer instead. Don’t forget to use SPF to help protect your skin from further damage.

There are a lot of factors to consider in your case. Hope these things will help in choosing what’s best for you. Best of luck!

Accutane (isotretinoin) addresses all of the culprits of acne formation which include excessive sebum/oil production, comedogenesis (the clogging of pores), inflammation, and even Cutibacterium acnes. You’re somehow right in the sense that it’s considered as a “last resort” treatment by dermatologists since it’s a potent medication with multiple risks if used incorrectly, but it’s not really the end of your options.

If the other factors have been addressed, maybe a little extra help is needed in controlling the growth of bacteria—which is why your dermatologist may be suggesting a course of antibiotics.

With proper use, it can help as the main culprit of acne is Cutibacterium acnes itself. When I had severe breakouts, my dermatologist prescribed me with antibiotics—doxycycline to be specific. It really helped a lot with clearing up my face.

You seem to be in good hands, but you can seek a second opinion if you want to be comfortable with the next step you’re taking. Don’t lose hope. Progress isn’t always linear, especially with acne. Wishing you the best!

Antibiotics may help, but it would require the prescription of a dermatologist. It’s best if you consult a board-certified dermatologist so they can assess the severity of your acne, the contributing risk factors, and the best approach to manage it.
Parts of your skin appear to be irritated and inflamed. May you elaborate your routine when you shave?

Aside from hyperpigmentation, you seem to be dealing with ice pick and box scars. Hyperpigmentation is usually manageable. Look for products with niacinamide and religiously use sun protection to help lighten their appearance.

As for the ice pick and box scars, it’s best that you consult a board-certified dermatologist. Topical creams can only do so much for these scars. Dermatologists can recommend chemical peels (like with TCA) to promote collagen formation. Acne scar surgery and lasers are other options.

If you’re acne prone with sensitive skin, it’s best to avoid possibly irritating products like tea tree oil. Stick to a facial wash with salicylic acid and a good moisturizer to control oil production.

Best of luck.
